statement: Find the maximum value of $5\cos\theta+12\sin\theta$ and a value of $\theta$ in $[0,2\pi)$ at which it is attained.
solution:
Write $5\cos\theta+12\sin\theta=R\cos(\theta-\alpha)$ where $R=\sqrt{5^2+12^2}=13$, $\cos\alpha=\tfrac{5}{13}$ and $\sin\alpha=\tfrac{12}{13}$. Hence
$$5\cos\theta+12\sin\theta=13\cos(\theta-\alpha).$$
The maximum value is $13$, attained when $\cos(\theta-\alpha)=1$, i.e. $\theta=\alpha$. So one such value is $\theta=\alpha$ with $\tan\alpha=\tfrac{12}{5}$ (approximately $1.176$ rad).
hints: Express as R cos(θ-α) with R=sqrt(5^2+12^2).
